title: Text filters behind an interface
hints: Interface methods are public, so each `apply` you write must be `public String apply(String text)`.
`Pipeline` implements `Iterable<TextFilter>` by returning its list's iterator; that is all an enhanced `for` needs.

A class written inside another class with `static`, like `static class Trim implements TextFilter { ... }` inside `class Filters { }`, is a **nested class**. It works like any other class; code outside names it `Filters.Trim`, as the tests do with `new Filters.Trim()`.

A `Map<String, String>` stores pairs from a key to a value (maps are covered in lesson 4.02); `Map.of("teh", "the")` makes one. `replacements.getOrDefault(word, word)` gives the replacement for `word`, or `word` itself when it has none. Split the text with `split(" ")`, replace each word, and put it back together with `String.join(" ", words)`.
